assets.name: lecture_09_frame_01.png
assets.rationale: The kinetic and potential terms are identifiable, but the lecturer blocks the center and the left edge clips part of the Hamiltonian. The complete expression is typeset instead.
assets.caption_hint: The nonrelativistic field Hamiltonian with kinetic and external-potential terms.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The potential energy is the integral of all space, the density of particles at point x times the potential at that point x.

assets.name: lecture_09_frame_02.png
assets.rationale: The four-field contact term and the meeting-point spacetime sketch remain visible together. The adjacent TikZ reconstruction removes the lecturer occlusion and labels the process cleanly.
assets.caption_hint: A local electron-proton contact interaction at a single spacetime point.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Interactions involving products of fields represent these basic simple interactions where particles, if they're at the same point, can interact with each other.

assets.name: lecture_09_frame_03.png
assets.rationale: The equation H = alpha P and the diagonal two-component spatial derivative are the clearest available statement of the massless left-right construction.
assets.caption_hint: The massless two-component equation with alpha distinguishing right and left movers.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Since alpha has both positive and negative eigenvalue, this describes both right moving and left moving waves.

assets.name: lecture_09_frame_04.png
assets.rationale: The conditions alpha squared = 1 and beta squared = 1 are visible, but the lecturer covers the anticommutator while it is being completed. The verified algebra is typeset from the full board sequence.
assets.caption_hint: The Dirac-matrix conditions while the anticommutator is still being written.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: We want that alpha beta plus beta alpha is equal to zero.

assets.name: lecture_09_frame_05.png
assets.rationale: Both orientations of the A to B plus C vertex are visible and legible during the second-order scattering construction.
assets.caption_hint: The elementary decay and recombination vertices used to build a second-order process.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: It takes a B and a C and turns it into an A, and then it takes the A, annihilates the A, and puts back a B and a C.

assets.name: lecture_09_frame_06.png
assets.rationale: The two-vertex exchange diagram is visible while the internal C line and external A and B lines are identified. The adjacent TikZ diagram supplies an unobstructed reconstruction.
assets.caption_hint: A and B scattering through exchange of C.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Now you have a scattering amplitude where A and B scatter with each other with the exchange of a C.

assets.name: lecture_09_frame_07.png
assets.rationale: The nonrelativistic and relativistic dispersion relations and c = 1 are centered, complete, and unobstructed enough to mark the lecture's pivot to the Dirac problem.
assets.caption_hint: The transition from nonrelativistic to relativistic energy-momentum relations.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: E squared is equal to p squared plus m squared. Now I've set the speed of light equal to one.

assets.name: lecture_09_frame_08.png
assets.rationale: Both coupled component equations are complete and legible; the lecturer stands to the left without obscuring the derivative or mass terms.
assets.caption_hint: The one-dimensional massive Dirac equation written as two coupled chiral components.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Once you introduce the mass term, the two components are not independent anymore; the equation couples one to the other.
